title: Lewis Dumaine, Gus Metcalf band and the Hall brothers
summary: He describes cornetist Lewis Dumaine, the band with Edmond Hall and others, and Hall's brothers Robert and Herbert.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel

blocks.x: Let's see. Ask him if he ever knew Lewis Dumain.

Did you know Lewis Dumain? Know who? Dumain. Oh, he's a baby Lewis Dumain. He's a professor, I mean a good reader. He couldn't jazz. He used to like to jazz but he could play nothing new and he could take a violin for it. Turn it upside down and play it all and put it in his keys. He could write through the range. He used to help me out a whole lot too with music. August Ruchel, that is a trambon player. When was he with Dumain? When was he with Dumaine? When was you with Dumaine?

When did you play with Dumaine? Let me see when that was. Twenty-something years ago, I think. We used to play with the same band, Gus Muscat. Now let's figure out how else about him. Gus Muscat. He was a baratone man.
Edmund Hall talks about him. Edmund Hall talks about him. Edmund Hall, Lee Cotting, T-Ball, Joe Rene. Let's see who else. We had a band.
Who was a trombone player? That's what I'm trying to take now. Whose band was it?
That's the one, yeah. Whose band was it?

It was Eddie. Eddie Hall. We called him Edmund Hall. Edmund Hall. Then I used to play with his brother, too. That's what I played at the country club. Which brother? That was Robert. Robert Hall. Oh, yes. And he got another brother named Claren. I know him. And he got another brother. He got about four or five brothers. Herbert. Herbert is, one plays guitar, too. One plays a saxophone. All three of them play saxophone.
Herbert Hall is in New York now. Yeah. Herbert Hall, he's doing well, the other brother.
He was, what's his name? Benny Goodwin, eh? Benny Goodwin, you know, the white fella. Yeah. He gave every soul a good name.
He gives Edmund a good name, yeah. Yeah. Let's see. He's on a record with me.

Yeah, who are? Edmund, yeah. And Rowland, you remember Rowland? That type of person ever that place? Somebody's up the line, not far from, uh. Chicago? Huh? Not far from Chicago? No, no, I mean, not up in the country, yeah. Oh. That's his room. Rowland. Forget you there, son. He's a good trumpet player, too. He used to play with Edmund and all of them up there, you know? Reserve. Reserve? Huh? Up at Reserve? Yeah, Reserve. Yeah, yeah, that's where they're from.
Yeah, that's where they're from. Yeah, that's where they're from.
